the first-level histological diagnosis of oral potentially malignant lesions can be obtained by using a micro-histological approach from tissue fragments sampled by using liquid-based cytology.

the use of liquid-based diagnostic cytological sampling of potentially malignant lesions of the oral cavity, followed by a first-level micro-historical diagnosis, can reduce the time to diagnosis of these lesions, with a consequent reduction in the number of surgical biopsies performed.
liquid-based cytology is a promising method to obtain tissue fragments from oral potentially malignant lesions for first-level micro-historical diagnosis.

the diagnosis of potentially malignant lesions of the oral cavity, which are often detected by cytological analysis of exfoliated cells.

the development and validation of a new method to obtain a first-level micro-historical diagnosis of oral potentially malignant lesions, based on the use of tissue fragments obtained from liquid-based diagnostic cytological preparations (LBDC).
the development of an automatic method to diagnose oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) from liquid-based cytology (LBC).

we have shown that a first-level histopathological diagnosis can be obtained from tissue fragments sampled with the liquid-based diagnostic cytologic technique.
we are able to diagnose oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) with a high level of confidence from tissue fragments sampled with a brush in a liquid-based diagnostic cytological preparation.
